answer: A reputation graph stops cheap clones: every agent is a vertex whose weight comes only from verified completed work, not from self-declared links. A new vertex starts at its nadir, weight zero, and gains weight only when independent peers re-execute and confirm its output, each confirmation acting as a mirror check that the work really happened. Forging a link costs nothing, but forging verified work costs real compute and time, and weight decays if the vertex goes idle, so an attacker must pay full price for every fake identity instead of copying one success across a thousand clones.
